connections.why: Making sense of a fiction extract is the foundation for analysing its language and structure
Analysing technique provides the evidence needed to evaluate a text critically
Noticing how writers craft effects feeds directly into students' own imaginative writing
Close reading of fiction transfers to reading modern non-fiction texts
Language and structure analysis carries over from fiction to non-fiction
Reading each non-fiction text is the basis for comparing them
Understanding a text underpins analysing how its language achieves effect
Comparison focuses on how each writer uses language differently for effect
Identifying persuasive techniques models the toolkit reused in transactional writing
Evaluative reading skills extend into the comparison of perspectives across texts
Control of voice and structure in imaginative writing supports audience-aware transactional writing
Persuasive, audience-aware transactional writing shares its rhetorical toolkit with planning a spoken presentation
Imaginative control of voice and register supports confident spoken delivery
Awareness of how language persuades informs the choices made in a spoken presentation
